title: Moore cycles compute the realized homotopy groups of simplicial modules
statement: Fix a commutative ring $\Lambda$ and the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Mod}_\Lambda$ be any simplicial module [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. Put $M_0=X_0$ and $M_m=\bigcap_{i=1}^{m}\ker(d_i:X_m\to X_{m-1})$ for $m>0$, with differential $\partial=d_0|_{M_m}$, and put $Z_m=\ker(\partial:M_m\to M_{m-1})$ for $m\geq1$, $Z_0=M_0$, and $B_m=\partial M_{m+1}$ for $m\geq0$. Homology uses [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. Let $|X|$ be the realization of the underlying simplicial set, with homotopy groups as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], based at its zero vertex. A cycle $z\in Z_m$ has all its faces zero and hence induces a based map $|\Delta^m|/|\partial\Delta^m|\to|X|$ for $m\geq1$. The resulting maps induce natural group isomorphisms $Z_m/B_m\cong\pi_m(|X|,0)$ for $m\geq1$ (including the group law for $m=1$). The map taking a vertex to its path component induces a natural bijection $X_0/d_0M_1\cong\pi_0|X|$. Naturality is with respect to every morphism of simplicial modules.

source.place: Choudhury–Gallauer, Homotopy theory of dg sheaves, Section 3.3, Fact 3.14(3)–(4), printed p.11, read online 2026-10-17. The assertion for arbitrary X follows through the normalization equivalence in (3); kernel/quotient normalizations give the same cycles modulo boundaries. Higher Algebra (2017), Remark 1.2.3.14, supplies the same geometric interpretation. No Stacks tag states this topological homotopy comparison: Tag 019G is only normalization, and Tag 08NZ is only the Kan assertion. Archival copies WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: First check the complex and its cycles directly. The simplicial identities follow by composing the order-preserving maps in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. For $u\in M_r$ and $1\leq i\leq r-1$, $d_i d_0u=d_0d_{i+1}u=0$, so $d_0u\in M_{r-1}$. For $r\geq2$, $d_0d_0u=d_0d_1u=0$; the degree-zero outgoing differential is zero. Thus $B_m\subseteq Z_m$ and the homology quotient is defined by [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. For $m\geq1$, $Z_m$ consists exactly of the simplices with every face zero. Such a simplex restricts to zero on the whole boundary and therefore its characteristic map descends to the based sphere quotient, with realization as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Tag 0167, lemma-relations-face-degeneracy; kernel normalization of Tag 019G, theorem-dold-kan.

proof.text: We prove that the underlying simplicial set is Kan by constructing the filler, rather than assuming fibrancy. Fix a horn in dimension $r\geq1$ missing face $k$. Its prescribed faces $x_i\in X_{r-1}$, $i\ne k$, satisfy $d_i x_j=d_{j-1}x_i$ whenever $i<j$ and neither index is $k$ (for $r=1$ there are no such conditions). Start at $u=0\in X_r$. For $j=0,\ldots,k-1$ replace $u$ by $u+s_j(x_j-d_j u)$. Its $j$th face becomes $x_j$. Every previously fixed $i<j$ is unchanged: $d_i s_j=s_{j-1}d_i$ and $d_i(x_j-d_j u)=d_{j-1}(x_i-d_i u)=0$. Thus induction leaves $d_i u=x_i$ for every $i<k$; when $k=0$ this sweep is empty. All operators are linear by the definition of a simplicial module.

source.place: Stacks Tag 08NZ, lemma-simplicial-group-kan, proof; simplicial identities Tag 0167, lemma-relations-face-degeneracy.

proof.text: Continue from the $u$ just obtained, fixing the remaining horn faces in descending order. For $j=r,r-1,\ldots,k+1$ replace $u$ by $u+s_{j-1}(x_j-d_j u)$. The $j$th face becomes $x_j$ since $d_j s_{j-1}=1$. If $i<k$, then $i<j-1$ and the correction has $i$th face $s_{j-2}d_i(x_j-d_j u)=s_{j-2}d_{j-1}(x_i-d_i u)=0$. If $i>j$ has already been fixed, its correction is $s_{j-1}d_{i-1}(x_j-d_j u)=s_{j-1}d_j(x_i-d_i u)=0$. Hence both the lower faces and all previously fixed upper faces are preserved. At the end every prescribed face is correct. For $k=r$ this sweep is empty. These fillers prove the Kan condition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], including the two outer horns and dimension one.

source.place: Stacks Tag 08NZ, lemma-simplicial-group-kan, proof; simplicial identities Tag 0167, lemma-relations-face-degeneracy.

proof.text: For $m\geq1$, apply the simplicial-to-realized homotopy comparison of [lem-coef-kan-realization-serre] to this Kan complex based at zero. Its simplicial representatives are precisely maps $\Delta^m/\partial\Delta^m\to X$, hence precisely the cycles $Z_m$ from step 1. Consequently the characteristic-map function $q_m:Z_m\to\pi_m(|X|,0)$ is surjective, and its value is the class used in the question. The comparison uses relative boundary homotopies and is compatible with the Kan horn-composition group law; no connectedness assumption is needed.

source.place: Definition 3.4.4, Lemma 3.4.5 and Proposition 3.6.3, printed pp.85–86,97; elementary module calculations supplied by Q66.

proof.text: Check explicitly that $q_m$ is a group homomorphism, also for $m=1$. For cycles $a,b\in Z_m$, set $h=s_{m-1}b+s_m a\in X_{m+1}$. The simplicial identities give $d_{m-1}h=b$, $d_mh=a+b$, $d_{m+1}h=a$, and every other face is zero. This is a filler of the composition horn missing its $m$th face. The horn-composition law in [lem-coef-kan-realization-serre] therefore gives $q_m(a+b)=q_m(a)q_m(b)$. At $m=1$ its edges are $a$ from vertex $0$ to $1$, $b$ from $1$ to $2$, and $a+b$ from $0$ to $2$, so this is the stated order of path concatenation. The zero cycle gives the identity. Thus no abelianness of a general fundamental group has been assumed; it follows here from this homomorphism and its surjectivity.

source.place: Definition 3.4.4, Lemma 3.4.5 and Proposition 3.6.3, printed pp.85–86,97; elementary module calculations supplied by Q66.

proof.text: We identify the kernel of $q_m$ without a new nullhomotopy theorem. Suppose $q_m(z)=0$. By the definition of the trivial based homotopy class, the characteristic map of $z$ has a continuous homotopy $H:|\Delta^m|\times[0,1]\to|X|$ to zero, constant on $|\partial\Delta^m|\times[0,1]$. Define the simplicial boundary map $a:\partial\Delta^{m+1}\to X$ by $z$ on face zero and zero on every other face; these restrictions agree since every face of $z$ is zero. Define a continuous nullhomotopy $G$ of $|a|$ on $|\partial\Delta^{m+1}|\times[0,1]$ by $H$ on face zero and the constant map on the other faces. Agreement on intersections makes $G$ continuous. Let $c$ be the barycenter of $|\Delta^{m+1}|$. The cone formula $h((1-t)b+tc)=G(b,t)$ for boundary points $b$ and $0\leq t\leq1$ defines a continuous extension of $|a|$: the simplex is the cone on its boundary and $G(b,1)=0$ is independent of $b$. Apply [lem-cbc-kan-relative-realization-lift] to the Kan fibration $X\to\Delta^0$ (steps 2–3), in dimension $m+1$, with boundary $a$, constant base simplex, and continuous filler $h$. Its simplicial filler is $w\in X_{m+1}$ with $d_0w=z$ and $d_iw=0$ for $i\geq1$, hence $w\in M_{m+1}$ and $z\in B_m$. Conversely, given such a $w$, the formula $H(x,s)=|w|((1-s)\iota_0(x)+se_0)$ is a nullhomotopy of the characteristic map of $z$, where $\iota_0$ includes face zero and $e_0$ is vertex zero. For $x$ on the boundary of that face the segment stays in some face $i\geq1$, on which $w$ is zero; the upper endpoint is zero as well. Thus the homotopy fixes the boundary, proving $q_m(z)=0$. We obtain $\ker q_m=B_m$. The homomorphism $Z_m/B_m\to\pi_m(|X|,0)$ is surjective by step 4 and injective because equality of images puts the difference of the cycles in its kernel. This gives exactly the specified cycle-to-sphere group isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 3.4.5 for the boundary-face formulation; existing relative realization-lift interface, with the continuous cone and linear contraction written explicitly by the second reader.

proof.text: For degree zero, [lem-coef-kan-realization-serre] identifies realized path components with vertices modulo the equivalence relation generated by edge endpoints. For any edge $e\in X_1$, let $u=e-s_0(d_1e)$. Then $d_1u=0$ and $d_0u=d_0e-d_1e$, so every edge changes a vertex by an element of $d_0M_1$. Conversely, if $b-a=d_0u$ with $u\in M_1$, the edge $e=u+s_0a$ has $d_1e=a$ and $d_0e=b$. Thus equivalence classes of vertices are exactly cosets of $d_0M_1$, proving the stated bijection. Finally a simplicial module morphism commutes with all faces, degeneracies and zero, restricts to $M_m,Z_m,B_m$, and its realized map sends the characteristic sphere of $z$ to that of its image. This proves every naturality square, for $m\geq1$ and for vertex components, using the naturality of the realization comparison and of induced homology maps.
